passage: Thomas's diary, Thursday. Asked Chinmay today if he wanted to join my cricket team. He lifted one shoulder and said, “Maybe.” I thought that meant no, and I felt a bit silly for asking. Then I remembered that he does the one-shoulder thing when he's unsure or shy. So I asked, “Do you want to think about it, or is cricket not your thing?” He said, “I've never really played. I don't want to be bad.” I said I'd show him how to hold the bat at recess. He said, “Okay, maybe yes.” 🙂

qa.q: What did Chinmay say after lifting one shoulder?
qa.a: He said, “Maybe.”

qa.q: What did Thomas first think Chinmay's shoulder lift meant, and what did asking reveal?
qa.a: He first thought it meant no. Asking revealed that Chinmay was unsure and worried about being bad, since he had never really played.

qa.q: What small step helped clear up the maybe?
qa.a: Thomas asked a friendly, open question and offered to show him how to hold the bat, so Chinmay could say what was holding him back.

qa.q: How might Chinmay feel about being asked?
qa.a: Probably relieved that Thomas asked kindly and did not push, since he admitted his worry about being bad.

grounding: A one-shoulder lift is a weak signal of uncertainty or shyness; asking clarifies.

passage: At the village school, Nitin asked Hafsa if she wanted to fly kites with him on the roof after class for Sankranti. Hafsa lifted one shoulder and looked at her sandals. “Maybe.” Nitin wasn't sure. Was it a no, or a yes? Her cheeks looked pink, and she wasn't walking away. “Do you want me to bring an extra kite for you?” he asked. Hafsa glanced up. “I don't know how to launch it.” “I'll show you,” said Nitin. Her shoulder dropped, and she nodded.

qa.q: What holiday did Nitin ask Hafsa about the kites for?
qa.a: He asked her to fly kites for Sankranti.

qa.q: What might Hafsa's one-shoulder lift have meant, and what else could it be?
qa.a: Likely uncertainty or shyness about not knowing how to launch a kite, since she looked at her sandals and her cheeks were pink. It could also have been a half-hearted maybe that meant no.

qa.q: What did Nitin do that helped clear things up?
qa.a: He noticed she was not walking away, and he asked a friendly question that offered help, so she told him what worried her.

qa.q: How might Hafsa feel when Nitin offers to show her?
qa.a: Probably relieved and a bit less shy, since her shoulder dropped and she nodded.

grounding: A one-shoulder lift is a weak signal of shyness or uncertainty; asking clarifies.

passage: At recess in their Singapore school, Mei handed Noa a folded invitation. “My birthday, Saturday. Will you come?” Noa read it and lifted one shoulder, just a little. Mei's smile wobbled. That's a no. She doesn't want to. She almost took the card back. Then she remembered her mum saying a shrug can mean a hundred things. “Is that a yes, a no or an I don't know?” Noa looked at her shoes. “I want to. It's just, it's a sleepover, and I've never slept away from home.” “Oh! You could come for the cake and go home before bed?” This time both of Noa's shoulders went up, in a happy bounce.

qa.q: What day was Mei's birthday party?
qa.a: Mei's birthday party was on Saturday.

qa.q: What was Mei feeling when Noa lifted one shoulder?
qa.a: Mei felt hurt and disappointed, reading the small shrug as a no.

qa.q: What did asking reveal?
qa.a: It showed Noa wanted to come but felt nervous about sleeping away, so they found a way she could join for the cake.

qa.q: What was the invitation like for Noa?
qa.a: Noa felt torn, wanting to go but nervous about a first night away from home, which the half-shrug showed.

grounding: Shows a child reading a friend's one-shoulder lift as a no, and asking to find it meant uncertainty.

passage: At the Sunday football club, Deepak, captain for the day, needed a goalkeeper. “Deepika, will you go in goal?” Deepika lifted one shoulder and looked sideways at the posts. Deepak nearly shouted, “Great, go!” and ran off to sort the others. Then he stopped. One shoulder wasn't really a yes. “Is that a maybe?” Deepika rubbed her arm. “Last time I dived, I scraped my whole elbow. And everyone saw when I let in three.” Deepak thought. “Do the first half as defender, then? Asha can start in goal.” Deepika nodded, properly this time, and jogged to the back.

qa.q: How many goals did Deepika let in last time?
qa.a: She let in three.

qa.q: What was Deepika feeling when she lifted one shoulder?
qa.a: She felt nervous and unsure, remembering the scraped elbow and everyone seeing the three goals.

qa.q: Why was asking “Is that a maybe?” wise?
qa.a: A one-shoulder lift is a weak signal, so asking brought out her worry and let Deepak offer a better position 👍

qa.q: What would change if Deepak had taken the shrug as a yes?
qa.a: Deepika might have gone in goal feeling scared and embarrassed, and Deepak would never have learned why she hesitated.

grounding: Shows a child reading a teammate's one-shoulder lift as a half-hearted maybe, and asking to clarify it.

passage: I'm Yogesh, and I sit with Baljeet in the back row. Yesterday Baljeet asked the new girl, Ritu, if she wanted to join our quiz team. Ritu lifted one shoulder and kept her eyes on her pencil box. Baljeet turned to me. “See? She's not interested.” I didn't know either. It could have meant anything. But Baljeet went back and asked, “Is that a no, or are you just not sure yet?” Ritu said quietly, “I'm not good at quizzes. I didn't want to let you down.” Baljeet said we mostly just guess anyway. She laughed and joined. I don't know what made Baljeet go back, but I'm glad.

qa.q: What did Baljeet ask Ritu to join?
qa.a: Baljeet asked Ritu to join their quiz team.

qa.q: What was Ritu feeling when she lifted one shoulder?
qa.a: Ritu felt unsure and worried about letting the team down, not uninterested.

qa.q: Which of Baljeet's choices worked, and why?
qa.a: Going back and asking what the shrug meant worked, because it brought out Ritu's worry so it could be answered.

qa.q: How did Yogesh read the shrug?
qa.a: Yogesh wasn't sure and thought it could mean anything, so there was no easy answer for Baljeet.

grounding: Shows a child reading a new classmate's one-shoulder lift as disinterest, then asking and finding shyness and doubt.

passage:
Monday: "Come to the dance audition with me?" Shalini asked. Seema lifted one shoulder and looked at her shoelaces. Shalini grinned. That's a yes. She wrote both their names on the list.

Wednesday: The audition started. Seema wasn't there. Shalini danced alone, cheeks hot, glancing at the door every few seconds.

Friday: At the bus stop Shalini couldn't hold it in. "You said you'd come!"
Seema's face crumpled. "I didn't say anything. I shrugged. I meant I didn't know. Everyone stares at you on that stage."
Shalini was quiet. "Next time I'll just ask again, properly."
"Next time," Seema said, "maybe just the practice, not the stage?"

qa.q: Whose names did Shalini write on the list?
qa.a: Both their names, hers and Seema's.

qa.q: What was Seema likely feeling when she lifted one shoulder and looked at her shoelaces?
qa.a: Unsure and shy about dancing in front of people, as she explains later; the shrug was a hesitant maybe, not a yes.

qa.q: What went wrong, and what could fix it next time?
qa.a: Shalini read a weak half-shrug as a yes; simply asking again, "Is that a yes?", would have cleared it up.

qa.q: What would change if Seema had said her worry out loud on Monday?
qa.a: Shalini would not have signed her up or felt let down, and they could have found an easier step together, like the practice.

grounding: It shows a child reading a friend's one-shoulder lift as a yes when it meant uncertainty and shyness, and learning to ask.
